newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Thousands bid farewell to Brazil's revered friar.
newsitem.headline: Thousands bid farewell to Brazil's revered friar.

text.p: Tens of thousands of Brazilians paid their last respects to a friar they considered a semi-saint on Wednesday, lining streets to see his coffin pass by on a fire truck and packing a soccer stadium for a funeral mass.

Worshippers who braved tropical heat to fill the 80,000-capacity Arruda stadium in the northeastern city of Recife waved white hankerchiefs as a final farewell to Friar Damiao, a Capuchin monk who died on Saturday, aged 98.

He was due to be buried later in the day in a private ceremony restricted to fellow monks and other Catholic dignitaries. The decision upset the plans of former President Fernando Collor who travelled from Miami to attend the funeral.

"This is very strange," Collor told national Globo television on hearing the news. He was often photographed helping the stooped monk, one of his staunchest supporters, before resigning in a corruption scandal in 1992.

Born Pio Gianotti in the Italian city of Bozzano, Damiao arrived in Brazil in 1931 and spent 66 years touring the vast and arid northeast mostly on foot to bring the Bible to remote towns and villages.

He used to warn the faithful that hell was waiting for adulterers, communists and even people who danced. Despite his strict views, he was revered by the rural poor and thousands of people would turn out to see and touch him wherever he went.

President Fernando Henrique Cardoso declared Wednesday an official day of mourning. About 100,000 people waited in long lines to file past the friar's open coffin between Sunday and Tuesday, news reports said.
